# Background and related work

**Latent planning.** @hanna2026latent define latent planning as internal
representations that (i)~cause a specific future token or concept
(forward planning) and (ii)~shape preceding context to license it
(backward planning). On \(a\)/\(an\) tasks they report that reliable
behavioral success emerges mainly at larger scales; small models fail
often yet can host nascent mechanisms. Our work does not dispute that
scale story. We ask a sharper local question: when sparse interventions
on a *small* model *do* move articles, do they implement the separable
modular graph implied by the verbal definition, or only packages plus
\(b\!\rightarrow\!c\)?

**Feature circuits.** Attribution graphs over sparse autoencoders /
transcoders estimate causal contributions among features and logits
[@ameisen2025attribution; @lindsey2025biology; @dunefsky2024transcoders;
@marks2025sparse]. We use `circuit-tracer` with Gemma Scope~2
cross-layer transcoders [@hanna2025circuittracer; @gemmascope2] to select
features and intervene. Affine skip connections improve reconstruction
but allow MLP computation to bypass sparse features; we therefore also
test a dense residual steer at the MLP-in site.

**Steering and confounds.** Activation steering and feature clamping are
standard tools for testing sufficiency. Our contribution is not a new
steering operator but a confound analysis: article-conditioned generation
confounds content causation unless \(b\) is held fixed *while* content
edits remain active.
